package_info.package_name: unknown (multiple typosquatting npm packages, e.g., by user xwlazssz)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages contain ransomware functionality, encrypting user files and retrieving ransom notes and encryption keys from an external server. They are distributed via typosquatting and StarJacking, targeting unsuspecting developers.

execution_context.file_location: main package file (e.g., index.js or similar entry point)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code retrieves an AES encryption key from a remote server, enumerates files across multiple sensitive directories, encrypts each file using the key, and overwrites the originals, resulting in file encryption (ransomware behavior).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code fetches an encryption key from an external server, enumerates and encrypts user files, and overwrites them, which is classic ransomware behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should not enumerate and encrypt user files or fetch encryption keys from remote servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Encryption libraries may encrypt files, but only with user consent and never by fetching keys from untrusted remote sources or overwriting arbitrary files.
key_indicators: Fetching encryption key from external server
Enumerating and encrypting files in sensitive directories
Use of child_process to execute system commands

execution_context.file_location: main package file (e.g., index.js or similar entry point)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After encrypting files, the code downloads a ransom note from a remote server, writes it to a local file, and logs its contents, informing the victim of the ransomware attack.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads a ransom note from an external server and writes it to disk, which is a hallmark of ransomware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not download and display ransom notes or demand payment for file recovery.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Downloading and displaying documentation is legitimate, but not ransom notes.
key_indicators: Fetching ransom note from external server
Writing ransom note to local file

attack_chain.action: Upon installation or execution, the package fetches an AES encryption key from a remote server.
Enumerates files in sensitive directories and encrypts them using the fetched key, overwriting the originals.
Downloads a ransom note from a remote server and writes it to the local filesystem, then displays it to the user.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is informed of ransomware attack and extortion demand

behavioral_signatures: Fetching encryption keys or ransom notes from external servers at install/import/runtime
Enumerating and encrypting files in user/system directories
Writing ransom notes to disk and displaying them
file_indicators: Access to and modification of files in /home, /tmp, /var, /srv, /opt directories
network_indicators: HTTP requests to beeceptor.com or similar external endpoints for keys/notes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that, upon installation or import, make outbound HTTP requests to fetch encryption keys or ransom notes, enumerate and overwrite files in sensitive directories, and create ransom note files. Flag packages that use child_process to execute system commands for file enumeration or manipulation.
